newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude - Prompt light grades still depressed.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude - Prompt light grades still depressed.

text.p: Tighter supplies will lend some support to Asia's light crudes in August, but the prompt July market remains bearish, traders said on Monday.

Planned maintenance works at Australia's Cossack crude field in August will cut the spot availabilities of the crude, while the natural decline of Papua New Guinea's Kutubu crude field will also reduce output in August.
But an end-July Kutubu cargo was still on offer, with price discussion centred around Tapis APPI -90 cents per barrel.
Kutubu usually trades around Tapis -60/70, but limited demand in July had kept levels weak.
An end July/early August Labuan cargo traded end last week at OSP even was widely heard to have gone to a refiner in Malaysia.
On heavy crudes, August trading was thin, although sentiment remained bullish as high temperatures in Japan lead traders to expect continued good buying from Japanese utilities.
Japanese utilities were to nominate their August requirements later this week, which traders said should give a clearer idea of demand.
Minas was last traded at ICP +48 for July, while August Duri was done at ICP +1.01, for burning in Japan.
Limited August spot Bach Ho was also heard available, after two cargoes were sold by separate shosha last week to refiners in Australia, at OSP +58/+60.

In Mideast crudes, Oman levels remained weak, with rumours heard that another August cargo was done at a discount of 2/3 cents under Dubai, by a European major to China, but this could not be confirmed.
Last week, an August Oman cargo was confirmed sold to a major at Dubai -10, the first time it has traded under Dubai.
A parcel of Umm Shaif was also confirmed done between a Europan major and a US major around ADNOC -22/23.
